fields: Never-marked islands set, sequencing (shared by the globe and the Law Sphere)
Genome-wide set of never-marked (constitutively unmethylated) CpG islands

The never-marked island set, one set read two ways: the Sequencing Globe asks WHERE (which islands and regions departed), IAM's Law Sphere asks HOW (stray writing against the writer's 1/(1 + D) with the meter, the eraser's clean-up, the hold at marked islands). Membership v2 uses the noise maps: a CpG is never marked only when every type's level sits below the threshold by more than its measured noise (counting noise from read halves; person-to-person noise from donor halves minus read halves). v2 counts: never-marked islands 293,980 at 0.20, 124,282 at 0.10, 4,039 at 0.05; domains 2,675,894; read in every cell's two halves 22,033,507. v1 (raw maximum) was 1,003,203 / 11,482,817, about 70 % and 77 % noise-made.

It enters the chain as 'located island gains': the reference island list against which an island gain level is scored, i.e. the baseline the globe and the Law Sphere both need before they can say a given island has gained marks it shouldn't have.

IAM's Law scores stray writing at islands against the write layer's 1/(1 + D) and the hold; that scoring is only meaningful if the 'never-marked' baseline is real rather than an artifact of measurement noise — the v1 raw-maximum count was shown to be mostly noise (about 70% and 77%), so a noise-corrected set was needed before gains could be trusted.
How it is obtained or computed

Computed by seq_halves.py on Google (iam-halves; bucket halves/) from 137 inputs, 48 cells. A CpG is kept only when every cell type's level sits below the threshold by more than its measured noise (counting from read halves, person-to-person from donor halves minus read halves); thresholds 0.20, 0.10 and 0.05 give the three counts. The working threshold is still to be set from the noise maps. Formula: island gain level against the island reference.

Genome-wide, at the never-marked islands and domains of the set (domains 2,675,894; 22,033,507 read in every cell's two halves). The globe's island layer (where) is owed, so it is not yet in the chain.

Sits in IAM's Law at the write layer (stray writes, 1/(1 + D)) and the hold step, but lf_section is 'open: not yet tied to the law' — it has not been assigned a long-form section. Status is open: basis is 'measured (atlas levels); threshold to be set from the noise maps', and in_chain is marked NO ('the globe's island layer (where) is owed').
open: not yet tied to the law

The set itself comes from the IAM Sequencing Atlas (57 cells; megakaryocytes left out, identification only), basis 'measured (atlas levels); threshold to be set from the noise maps'. The source field still reads 'v2 by measured noise owed', while the value field gives v2 counts.

fields: Predicted methylation-maintenance (held-mark) error for a region, used as the healthy baseline against which observed error is judged

The sample's own predicted held error, eps_pred(L), built from IAM-A's line (the law's held error as IAM-A's counter counts it intercept, the slope of IAM-A's line with loose share slope); the Sequencing Globe compares each 1,000-CpG region's actual held error against this prediction rather than a fixed external number.
It enters as the expectation that each region's held error is checked against; the expectation everywhere is that observed held error should be ≈ prediction.

The globe's job is WHERE the problem is located, so it needs a self-referenced expected value per region (the sample's own prediction) to know what counts as a departure rather than comparing against an arbitrary fixed target.
How it is obtained or computed

eps_pred(L) is computed from IAM-A's line: intercept 0.04454 (the held error set by the coin and the two-coin push, derived from M alone) read through the counter, plus a slope of 0.034625 per unit loose share, where L is the sample's own loose share: eps_pred(L) = firm + 0.034625 x L.
In 1,000-CpG regions across the genome, each drawn as an equal-area pixel on the globe.

IAM's Law, link 1d (the hold is the same rule, slow: the slow-write rule), long-form section 1d. That section gives held/lost = (x/2)/(1-(1-e^-x)/x) as one function of write slowness x; for the cell x = 2M = 41.88, giving odds 21.45 and intercept eps0 = 0.04454 (the held error set by the coin and the two-coin push, derived from M alone). The slope 0.034625 is only partly derived: the within-sample part comes from the pump and is derived, replicated in a second laboratory; status overall for this row is partly derived (the held error set by the coin and the two-coin push intercept derived, the slope of IAM-A's line with loose share slope partly).

Value as given: 0.04454 (the held error set by the coin and the two-coin push); the globe uses the sample's own prediction from IAM-A's line. Source/basis: partly derived (the held error set by the coin and the two-coin push intercept derived, the slope of IAM-A's line with loose share slope partly); source_kind: derived by IAM's Law (fixed by the physics; a setting only to test what-if).

fields: Background rate of spurious methylation marks at unmarked CpG sites (a write-error rate)
The expected level of stray marks where none belong: the writer sometimes puts a mark where none belongs, and choosing the right site over 60 wrong ones gives about one stray mark in 61.
It enters the Sequencing Globe's working as the expected stray level at unmarked regions - a baseline that is counted into the calculation rather than itself drawn as a point on the map.

The instrument compares each 1,000-CpG region's held error against the sample's own predicted held error; it needs this expected stray-mark baseline at unmarked regions to know what a region with no real signal should read.
How it is obtained or computed

u = 1/(1 + D) + meter, with D = 60: the write error alone is 1/61 = 0.0164 (before the meter), and the meter's own false-mark rate (the stray-mark rate after the meter's own false marks: meter = conv_fail + tc_err, about 0.0044 + 0.00046) is added to give the expected stray level the sequencer reads at unmarked regions. Basis: measured selection and meter.
Counted, not drawn: it is a genome-wide expected baseline at unmarked regions rather than a value plotted as its own point on the sphere map.

Enters IAM's Law at link 1 (actualization: each write is one sudden write of a record), long-form section 1, 'Step 1: actualization, the moment a bit becomes part of the record.' The Sequencing Globe needs to localize where maintenance fidelity departs, and IAM's Law (link 1d) ties the held/lost ratio directly to how sudden or slow a write is, so knowing which regions restore in bursts versus steadily would sharpen that localization.

fields: Coin, temperature, two coins (M = 20.94, SAM cost 2)

record.law: IAM's Law, step 1 (Actualization): a sudden write of an einselected pointer into a blank Gaussian surface splits the energy exactly: held = spent = U = k_BT times the two relative entropies. Status: DERIVED GIVEN the four write conditions (sudden, no opposing record, Gaussian, einselected). IAM's Law, step 1d (The maintained hold (the slow write)): held/lost = (x/2)/(1 - (1 - e^-x)/x); sudden x -> 0 kept = lost; the cell at x = 2M: odds 21.45, E_hold 3.066 kT, phi = 0.1464 ~ ln M/M. Status: DERIVED (identity). IAM's Law, step 2 (The price): each nat costs at least k_BT held and k_BT spent; k_BT ln 2 per bit is the floor, paid at the receiving surface's own T. Status: DERIVED (Landauer) for the floor. IAM's Law, step 2b (The funding): the payment is free energy degraded to heat, traced to the low-entropy start (ATP <- food <- sunlight; stars <- fusion and contraction). Status: DERIVED given the Past Hypothesis, which is a postulate of established physics too (gap 16, not closable). IAM's Law, step 5 (The arrow): per record, beta W_diss = U/k_BT >= chi; the arrow lives in the dropped coordinate (the Koide phase); a record that drops delta cannot be inverted. Status: DERIVED GIVEN the low-entropy start. IAM's Law, step 7 (The ledger): heat k_BT ln2 at a horizon adds exactly 4 ln2 l_P^2 (one tile). BOOKING SETTLED (register R13, HORIZON BOOKINGS): the book's booking, heat crossing at T_GH (eq:Sdot), is self-consistent with weight 1 and gives an IDENTICAL Friedmann equation with the Kodama-Hayward temperature inside the unified first law; it does not by itself produce Omega_m (beta_m is input, link 8). The TALLY (Misner-Sharp, booked at once) is real: each bit at exactly half, no signal needed; but its half is Smarr's degree-2 half, equal to the virial half only in D = 4, and the two bookings cannot both hold for a growing record; the book's phantom result needs the heat booking. Status: DERIVED for the tile and for both bookings' consistency.

Does the globe put an error bar or confidence band around each region's result so we know if a departure is real or just noise?

Not yet recorded: the rule calls for each site to get a 'healthy width' borrowed from the atlas's person-to-person spread (cells with one library borrowing their lineage's spread), but the limits note that this healthy bar is still owed and has not been delivered.

Why are regions defined as blocks of 1,000 CpGs instead of looking at single sites or smaller windows?

Because held error is rare (roughly 4%), a window needs about 1,000 CpGs to accumulate enough chances of a departure to clear the counting floor; smaller windows would not gather enough events to be statistically meaningful, and the packet does not give any finer resolution than this 1,000-CpG region (or 10-site block) scheme.
